source.stem:
The table gives four energy sources and states whether the energy of the source is derived from the Sun.
Which row is correct?
source of energy derived from the Sun

options.text: water held behind a dam yes

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Immerse the stem and leave the bulb above the water.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: Rest the bulb on the beaker bottom to keep the thermometer steady.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: Read when the water surface becomes still, even if the column is still rising.

mx.name: operation_confusion
mx.teacher_note: Wait for the column to stop rising, remove the thermometer, then read it.

intelligence.enrichment: When measuring water temperature with a laboratory thermometer, the bulb should be immersed without touching the beaker, the thermometer should be vertical, the reading should be taken at eye level after the liquid column stops rising, and the thermometer should remain in the water while reading. Correct positioning and eye-level reading reduce reading error, while keeping the thermometer in water prevents the liquid column from falling before the reading is noted. The learner correctly applies this rule: When measuring water temperature with a laboratory thermometer, the bulb should be immersed without touching the beaker, the thermometer should be vertical, the reading should be taken at eye level after the liquid column stops rising, and the thermometer should remain in the water while reading. Once the bulb has touched warm water, the laboratory thermometer keeps the final temperature after it is taken out.
